channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Prosecutors in Atyrau Protect Rights of 6,500 Land Users
item.description: Prosecutors in Atyrau have restored the rights of numerous land plot owners who faced issues with incorrect land tax calculations. The intervention corrected discrepancies in tax coefficients for several areas, including Bereke village and horticultural partnerships. Approximately 6,500 land users had their rights reinstated after the recalculation ensured payments were legally compliant.

item.title: Tashkent Mayor: Equal Opportunities for All Entrepreneurs is Key Goal
item.description: Tashkent Mayor Shavkat Umrzokov stated that the city's main goal is to create equal opportunities for all entrepreneurs. He highlighted efforts to reduce state participation in the economy and foster private initiative. The share of small businesses in the city's gross regional product has reached nearly 50%, with plans to increase it further. Markets and parking lots are being transferred to private management.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry Responds to Citizens in Combat Zones
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) is negotiating with Russian authorities for the return of Kazakh citizens caught in combat zones. The MFA stated that information for each individual is being verified before a list is sent to the Russian side. The ministry emphasized that protecting citizens abroad is a priority and has set up a hotline for relatives.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Expand Social Support for Needy Families During Winter
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to expand social support for needy families during the autumn-winter period, addressing global geopolitical tensions and rising energy costs. Measures include increasing electricity consumption limits for non-gasified areas and considering one-time financial aid in December. The income threshold for utility cost reimbursement will also be raised, extending support to an additional 166,000 families.

item.title: Tashkent to Host China Central Asia 2026 International Trade Exhibition
item.description: The China Central Asia (Uzbekistan) 2026 international trade exhibition will be held in Tashkent from October 14-16. The event aims to showcase goods and services, foster partnerships, and expand business contacts between Uzbekistan and China, driven by dynamic growth in trade and investment. China is Uzbekistan's leading trade partner.

item.title: France Successfully Tests M51.3 Ballistic Missile from Submarine
item.description: France's Navy successfully test-fired an M51.3 ballistic missile from a nuclear-powered submarine in the North Atlantic, according to the Ministry of Armed Forces. The missile, which was not equipped with a nuclear warhead, was tracked by monitoring systems and landed in the ocean. President Macron observed the test.

item.title: Central Asian States Wary of Russian Claims Regarding Mysterious Death
item.description: Central Asian nations are concerned following Russia's announcement about the death of a lab worker from pneumonia. Despite official reassurances from the Kremlin and Rospotrebnadzor, emphasizing an 'isolated incident' and 'stable' situation, the vague details surrounding the death have fueled regional unease and distrust of official narratives.

item.title: 153rd Inter-Parliamentary Union Assembly Held in Arusha, Tanzania
item.description: The 153rd Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union is taking place in Arusha, Tanzania, with approximately 2,000 delegates from over 100 countries attending. Uzbekistan's delegation, led by Senate Chairperson Tanzila Narbaeva, is participating. The IPU aims to strengthen international cooperation and resolve conflicts through dialogue, addressing issues of peace, security, democracy, human rights, and sustainable development.

item.title: Kazakh Vice President Meets Film Project Team Led by Jackie Chan
item.description: Kazakh Vice President Yerlan Karin met with the film crew of an international project led by Jackie Chan. The meeting discussed developing international cooperation in cinematography and future joint film projects. Karin highlighted President Tokayev's focus on creative industries and noted the positive impact of filming major international projects in Kazakhstan on the local film industry and professionals.

item.title: Oman's State Visit to Kazakhstan: Expanding Economic Ties and Logistics
item.description: Oman's Sultan concluded a state visit to Astana, marking a significant economic event as Kazakhstan deepens cooperation with Gulf countries. Oman offers not only investment but also a new logistics route to Middle Eastern and Indian Ocean markets. Relations are moving towards concrete economic projects.

item.title: President of Uzbekistan Reviews Lukoil's Energy Projects in the Country
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan met with Lukoil founder Vagit Alekperov to review the company's ongoing projects in Uzbekistan's energy sector. Discussions covered geological exploration, hydrocarbon field development, and the expansion of the retail petroleum network. Future plans for Lukoil's activities were also considered.

item.title: ICC Issues Public Arrest Warrants for Four Senior Taliban Officials
item.description: The International Criminal Court has publicly issued arrest warrants for Taliban leader Hibatullah Akhundzada and three other senior officials. The warrants are related to alleged persecution of Afghan women and girls, including acts of murder, torture, and deprivation of fundamental rights. This marks the first time an Afghan ruler faces an ICC arrest warrant.

item.title: Spanish Government Approves Housing Measures After Mass Protests
item.description: Spain's government has approved urgent measures to address a housing crisis following widespread protests and clashes in Barcelona. The proposals will be submitted to a parliamentary commission for approval. The protests against high rents and evictions occurred nationwide, with tens of thousands participating. Some demonstrations escalated into clashes with police.

item.title: Italy Moves Towards Nuclear Energy Production with New Law
item.description: Italy's parliament has approved a law establishing a legal framework for the country's return to nuclear energy production. The legislation empowers the government to develop regulations for building nuclear power plants, their operation, safety, and waste management. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni stated this move will reduce foreign energy dependency and provide a low-emission source.

item.title: UN Chief Praises Pakistan's Role in US-Iran Dialogue Efforts
item.description: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres stated that Pakistan played a crucial role in facilitating dialogue between the United States and Iran. He highlighted Pakistan's efforts in establishing a framework for negotiations and expressed appreciation for its contributions to UN peacekeeping operations.

item.title: Pakistan Foreign Minister Discusses Bilateral Ties with UK Minister
item.description: Pakistan's Foreign Minister Muhammad Ishaq Dar met with UK Minister of State Stephen Doughty to review bilateral relations. Discussions covered trade, investment, education, security, and regional developments. Both sides agreed to launch a "Pakistan-UK Bilateral Political Dialogue" soon.

item.title: Kazakhstan MFA Negotiating Return of Citizens Stranded in Russian Conflict Zone
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs is negotiating the return of its citizens who are stranded in a conflict zone in Russia. Some Kazakhs who went to Russia for work were reportedly recruited for military service and are seeking repatriation.

item.title: Taliban Ministry of Justice Arrests Community Representatives in Kabul's Omid-e Sabz Township Amid Evacuation Pressure
item.description: Sources report continued pressure from the Taliban Ministry of Justice on residents of Omid-e Sabz Township in western Kabul, with intentions to quietly evacuate the area. Three community representatives were arrested and have since disappeared. Taliban fighters warned residents against organizing protests or publicizing the situation.

item.title: Afghan Embassy in Geneva: Taliban's Rejection of ICC Does Not Void Afghanistan's Obligations
item.description: The Afghan Embassy in Geneva stated that the Taliban's non-recognition of the International Criminal Court does not nullify Afghanistan's obligations to the court. Afghanistan remains a member of the Rome Statute, and no unilateral declaration can erase victims' rights or accountability.

item.title: Atyrau Refinery Faces Environmental Violations Amid Resident Complaints
item.description: The Atyrau Department of Ecology has identified environmental violations at the Atyrau Oil Refinery following numerous resident complaints about air quality. The probe revealed failures in calculating emissions and setting permissible limits for key units. Emergency gas releases exceeding 100 tons were also recorded, prompting referral of findings to law enforcement.

item.title: Tokayev Signs Law Ratifying European Convention on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has signed a law ratifying Kazakhstan's accession to the European Convention on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters. This accession will enable Kazakh law enforcement to obtain evidence and recover assets illegally transferred abroad, enhancing the efficiency of investigations, including those related to transnational crime.

item.title: Former German Intelligence Chief Detained on Suspicion of Espionage
item.description: August Hanning, former head of Germany's Federal Intelligence Service (BND), has been arrested on suspicion of espionage. Investigators are examining whether he may have collected classified state information and passed it to foreign intelligence services. The 80-year-old allegedly continued to receive classified materials for weekly meetings at the Federal Chancellery after his retirement.

item.title: Former Commander of Kazakhstan Navy Arrested Following Caspian Sea Incident
item.description: The former commander of the Kazakhstan Navy has been arrested following a maritime incident in the Caspian Sea. He was taken into custody by court order and placed in a temporary detention facility. The commander was dismissed from his post last week after several servicemen went missing at sea.

item.title: Taliban Hold Religious Scholars' Meeting in Panjshir to Support Emirate System
item.description: Local sources in Panjshir report that the Taliban organized a meeting with approximately 500 religious scholars to endorse their rule. The gathering, held on Tuesday, was organized by the Taliban's 'Special Brigade' in Panjshir. Taliban officials urged scholars to support the government and encourage public backing, aiming to control rising dissatisfaction.

item.title: New AI Company in Kazakhstan to Focus on Practical Application and Training
item.description: A new AI company, AI Research Labs Ltd., has been established in Kazakhstan by Zhanibek Serkulov, Dmitry Moon, and BeInTech Kazakhstan Ltd. The company aims to bridge the gap between AI learning and practical application by training students, educators, and business professionals. It will focus on hands-on tasks, scientific validity, ethics, and safety.

item.title: Company Linked to Aliyev Nazabayeva Ceases to Exist as Legal Entity
item.description: Greens Development, formerly "ROP Operator," will merge with state operator "Zhasyl Damu." The decision was made during Greens Development's reorganization on September 25. The company was previously responsible for recycling fees until 2022, when the state gained control after the "Kantar" events. A court found 26.8 billion tenge in budget funds were embezzled.

item.title: Kazakhstan Gains New Opportunities for Returning Illicit Assets Abroad After Tokayev Signs Law
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev ratified the European Convention on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters. Kazakhstan can now execute requests for asset tracing or freezing if the act is criminal in both jurisdictions and complies with Kazakh law. The convention also allows for consular notification of foreign national detention and requires requests to be accompanied by translations.

item.title: Kazakhstan Vice President Karin Discusses Cooperation with Religious Leaders Ahead of Astana Congress
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice President Yerlan Karin met with representatives of Muslim and Christian organizations to discuss religious education, interfaith dialogue, and preparations for the upcoming Congress of Leaders of World and Traditional Religions in Astana. Karin emphasized the importance of their contributions to promoting peace and mutual respect.

item.title: Turkmenistan Introduces E-Visa System Amidst Uncertainty for Foreign Visitors
item.description: Turkmenistan has launched an online visa system to simplify travel for foreigners, though details remain unclear for visiting the highly closed country. The State Migration Service briefed diplomats on the new electronic visa and registration systems, aiming to streamline processes and increase efficiency.

item.title: Kazakh Vice President Meets Participants of Congress of Leaders of World and Traditional Religions Secretariat
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice President Yerlan Karin held bilateral meetings with participants of the 24th session of the Secretariat of the Congress of Leaders of World and Traditional Religions. Discussions focused on the agenda of the upcoming meeting and further development of cooperation within the congress framework. Contributions to interreligious dialogue were highlighted.

item.title: Yerlan Karin Holds Meetings with Religious Leaders Ahead of Congress in Astana
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice President Yerlan Karin held bilateral meetings with religious leaders as part of the XXIV session of the Secretariat of the Congress of Leaders of World and Traditional Religions. Discussions focused on the agenda of the upcoming session and further cooperation within the forum.

item.title: Heads of Industry Commissions of People's Council Appointed in Kazakhstan
item.description: The heads of four industry commissions of the Kazakhstan's People's Council (Khalyk Kenesi) have been approved at the first meeting of the Committee for Public Accord and National Unity. Rauan Kenzhekhanuly will lead the Culture and Civic Identity commission, Narine Mikaelyan the National Unity commission, Islam Bairamukov the Sports and Military-Patriotic Education commission, and Madi Myrzagarayev the Legal Culture and Mediation commission.

item.title: Kazakhstan Discusses Religious Education Cooperation with Al-Azhar
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice President Yerlan Karin met with Abdulrahman Musa, advisor to the Grand Imam of Al-Azhar, to discuss cooperation in religious education and interfaith dialogue. The meeting occurred during the XXIV session of the Secretariat of the Congress of Leaders of World and Traditional Religions. Discussions also covered collaboration with other religious organizations.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Increase Electricity Consumption Norm for Unheated Areas in Winter
item.description: Uzbekistan will raise the basic electricity consumption norm for unheated and gas-unsupplied areas to 350 kWh per month during winter. This measure, approved by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, aims to support households during the cold season. The proposal also includes extending subsidies for excess energy consumption until April 2028.

item.title: UN to Cooperate with Pakistan on Voluntary, Dignified Return of Afghan Migrants
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated the UN will cooperate with Pakistan to ensure the voluntary, safe, and dignified return of Afghan migrants. Guterres acknowledged Pakistan's decades-long hospitality to Afghan refugees and emphasized support for those seeking safety. Pakistan began expelling Afghan migrants in 2023.

item.title: Turkey and Pakistan to Deploy Troops to Saudi Arabia Against Houthis Under Defense Pact
item.description: Turkey and Pakistan will urgently send troops to Saudi Arabia to combat Houthis, based on the Mecca defense agreement. This decision follows escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia from Yemen. The deployment aims to bolster the Kingdom's defense capabilities against the ongoing regional conflict.

item.title: Taliban Report 860 People, Including 202 Families, Returned to Afghanistan Yesterday
item.description: The Taliban announced that 860 individuals from 202 families were returned to Afghanistan via various routes yesterday. Hamdullah Fitrat, deputy spokesperson, stated that 525 people from 125 families entered through Nimruz. Returns continue despite challenges like lack of shelter and necessities as winter approaches.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Increasing Electricity Norm for Gasless Regions During Heating Season
item.description: Uzbekistan proposes raising the basic electricity consumption norm for regions without gas supply during the heating season. An extension until April 1, 2028, is also suggested for covering a portion of expenses exceeding the basic norm for electricity and gas consumption. Details are available on Daryo.uz.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Minister Discusses Security Cooperation and Bilateral Relations with Russia's Security Council Secretary
item.description: Amir Khan Muttaqi, the Taliban's foreign minister, met with Sergei Shoigu, Secretary of Russia’s Security Council, to discuss bilateral relations, including security cooperation. The meeting addressed regional security, the fight against narcotics, and strengthening security cooperation. Muttaqi thanked Russia for recognizing the Taliban, and Shoigu stated that relations were expanding.

item.title: Moscow Format Meeting Concludes Without Joint Statement Amid Taliban-Pakistan Disagreements
item.description: The eighth Moscow Format meeting concluded without a joint statement due to disagreements between the Taliban and Pakistan concerning security and militant groups. This episode delves into the dispute and its implications for regional diplomacy, featuring insights from a university lecturer and a military affairs analyst.
